question: Which statement best describes Text-like inputs: text, email, password, tel, url, search?
options: checkbox is an independent on/off toggle — multiple can be checked, each submits its value only when checked. radio buttons sharing a name form a mutually exclusive group where exactly one can be selected. Use checkboxes for 'select any' and radios for 'select one of several'. Give each a value so the server knows which option was chosen.

number gives a spinner field that accepts only numeric input and supports min, max, and step; range is a slider for the same constrained value when the exact number matters less than the relative position. Both clamp to min/max and snap to step. Use number for precise entry (quantity, age) and range for fuzzy selection (volume, brightness).

These share a text field UI but differ in semantics and validation. email validates an email format and shows an email keyboard; password masks characters; url validates a URL; tel doesn't validate (formats vary) but triggers a phone keypad; search may show a clear button. Picking the right one gives free validation and the correct mobile keyboard.

type=date shows a native date picker and submits an ISO value (YYYY-MM-DD); related types include time, datetime-local, month, and week. type=color shows a color picker and submits a hex value (#rrggbb). These swap a fiddly text entry for a native, validated, locale-aware control with almost no code.
explanation: These share a text field UI but differ in semantics and validation. email validates an email format and shows an email keyboard; password masks characters; url validates a URL; tel doesn't validate (formats vary) but triggers a phone keypad; search may show a clear button. Picking the right one gives free validation and the correct mobile keyboard.
